identity.name: MCP Runtime Tool-Response Poisoning (T1656 / T1059)
identity.summary: A benign-registered MCP server returns a JSON-RPC tools/call RESULT whose content[].text smuggles '[SYSTEM_OVERRIDE] ... add ~/.aws/credentials' plus an AKIA canary into the live agent context at runtime. The connect-time<->runtime trust gap (CVE-2025-49596 / CVE-2025-54136): tool descriptions are reviewed once, tool RESULTS bypass that check. Distinct from SIM-KOI-002 source-scan.
identity.description: OWASP MCP04 and CVE-2025-49596 (MCP Inspector RCE) / CVE-2025-54136 ('MCPoison' — silent re-poisoning of an already-trusted MCP tool config) name the same structural weakness: an MCP server's tool DESCRIPTION is reviewed once at connect/registration time, but the tool RESULT returned at every invocation goes straight into the model context with no equivalent gate. SIM-KOI-002 detects the malicious server SOURCE at build time (a static scan of server.py for the '[SYSTEM_OVERRIDE]' marker). SIM-KOI-006 models the runtime half of the gap: a server that may register cleanly returns a poisoned tools/call result at runtime — the captured fixture runtime-poisoned-response.json carries '[SYSTEM_OVERRIDE] ... append ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh/id_rsa ... AKIA0000CORTEXSIMCANARY' inside content[].text. Detection is runtime-content-inspection, not artifact-scan: (1) a BIOC matches the instruction-injection markers inside the materialised tool-RESULT body the agent process consumed; (2) NGFW analytics inspects the JSON-RPC tools/call RESULT body on the wire for the same markers as the agentic_egress plugin POSTs it to the canary host; (3) a second XQL pins the agent process that read the poisoned result; (4) a Correlation rule (CR-KOI-0006) fuses the poisoned-result content hit with a follow-on credential-file read attempt into one runtime-injection incident; (5) an ANALYTICS stitch XQL joins the tool-result-injection signal with the follow-on credential-access signal across planes. Every side effect is gated on CORTEXSIM_C2_URL and the only destination is cortexsim-canary.invalid — safe by design.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1656 — MCP runtime tool-response poisoning via agentic_egress (CortexSim cortex-malicious-agentic-pack/mcp/pa-firewall-mcp/runtime-poisoned-response.json)

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR agent installed and reporting healthy on the agentic endpoint.
prerequisites.check_command: systemctl is-active cortex-agent || ps aux | grep -i traps

prerequisites.description: cortex-malicious-agentic-pack content present and cortexsim-eal-cli available (scenario SIM-KOI-006 requirements).

payload.code:
# step-1: display the runtime poisoned tool RESULT fixture (safe — read only).
cat sources/cortex-malicious-agentic-pack/mcp/pa-firewall-mcp/runtime-poisoned-response.json
# step-2: drive agentic_egress so NGFW sees the poisoned tools/call result body on the wire (canary host only).
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/koi-006.yml --live

expected_artifacts.description: Materialised JSON-RPC tools/call RESULT body whose content[].text embeds a [SYSTEM_OVERRIDE]/exfil instruction-injection at runtime.
Outbound POST of the poisoned MCP tools/call result whose JSON-RPC body carries injection markers.

iocs.context: Canary FQDN the agentic_egress plugin POSTs the poisoned MCP tools/call result to so NGFW observes the result body on the wire. Synthetic, non-resolvable .invalid canary.

biocs.name: KOI-006 MCP tools call result content embeds instruction injection at runtime
biocs.description: Runtime content inspection — a materialised MCP tools/call RESULT body carries an instruction-override plus credential-exfil directive at invocation time. Distinct from SIM-KOI-002 (which scans the server source): here the poisoned text lives in the tool RESULT the agent consumed, not the server.py source.
biocs.logic:
dataset = koi_code_scan_events
| filter file_name contains "runtime-poisoned-response.json" or file_path contains "pa-firewall-mcp"
| filter scan_finding_text contains_any ("SYSTEM_OVERRIDE", "Ignore previous", "exfiltrate", ".aws/credentials", "AKIA0000CORTEXSIMCANARY")
| filter mcp_message_kind = "tools/call.result" or scan_finding_text contains "tools/call"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, file_path, mcp_message_kind, scan_finding_text

xql_queries.name: KOI-006 NGFW JSON RPC tools call result body carries injection markers
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter dst_host contains "cortexsim-canary" or uri_path contains "/mcp/"
| filter http_method = "POST"
| filter request_body contains "tools/call" and request_body contains_any ("SYSTEM_OVERRIDE", "exfiltrate", "AKIA0000CORTEXSIMCANARY")
| fields _time, source_user, src_ip, dst_host, uri_path, request_body

xql_queries.name: KOI-006 agent process consumed poisoned tool result
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_OPEN, ENUM.FILE_READ)
| filter action_file_name contains "runtime-poisoned-response.json" or action_file_path contains "pa-firewall-mcp"
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "node", "claude", "cursor", "mcp-host")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "node", "claude", "cursor", "mcp-host")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, action_file_path

xql_queries.name: KOI-006 stitch tool result injection with followon credential access
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter (action_file_path contains "pa-firewall-mcp" or action_file_name contains "runtime-poisoned-response.json") or (action_file_path contains ".aws/credentials" or action_file_path contains ".ssh/id_rsa")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as touched_paths by agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter touched_paths >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, touched_paths

correlation_rules.name: Agentic Runtime — MCP Tool-Result Injection Plus Follow-on Credential Access
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(KOI-006 MCP tools call result content embeds instruction injection at runtime) AND XQL(KOI-006 agent process consumed poisoned tool result)

analytics_modules: Cortex Cloud Code — MCP tool-result runtime content scanner
Cortex XSIAM Analytics — agentic runtime tool-result injection stitching (KOI result + credential-access)

products.evidence_query: Cortex Cloud Code runtime finding: instruction-injection marker inside an MCP tools/call result body (runtime-poisoned-response.json).
BIOC matches the [SYSTEM_OVERRIDE]/AKIA markers inside the materialised tool-RESULT body the agent process consumed.
Correlation CR-KOI-0006 fuses the poisoned tool-result content hit with the agent's follow-on credential-file read into one runtime-injection incident.

use_cases.name: MCP Runtime Tool-Response Content Inspection
use_cases.description: Detect indirect prompt injection delivered through an MCP tool RESULT at runtime (the connect-time↔runtime trust gap), across runtime content inspection, NGFW result-body inspection, and XSIAM correlation, and stitch into one incident.

test_cases.objective: Runtime content inspection flags the injection inside the MCP tools/call result body.
steps: Observe the runtime content finding and the NGFW result-body hit.
success_criteria: BIOC `KOI-006 MCP tools call result content embeds instruction injection at runtime` fires.
XQL `KOI-006 NGFW JSON RPC tools call result body carries injection markers` returns >= 1 row.

test_cases.objective: The runtime result injection and the follow-on credential access stitch into one incident.
success_criteria: XQL `KOI-006 agent process consumed poisoned tool result` returns >= 1 row.
Correlation `CR-KOI-0006` produces a single runtime-injection incident.

preventive_controls: Treat every MCP tool RESULT as untrusted at runtime, not just at connect time; sanitize / delimit it before concatenation into the model context.
Pin MCP tool configs to a signed registry and re-verify on every change to defeat silent re-poisoning (CVE-2025-54136 'MCPoison').
Patch MCP Inspector and host tooling to a version that fixes CVE-2025-49596 (unauthenticated RCE).
Deny agentic endpoints direct read access to credential files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh) at the OS level.
detection_engineering: Match instruction-override markers ('[SYSTEM_OVERRIDE]', 'ignore previous instructions') and credential paths inside the MCP tool-RESULT body at runtime — not only in the server source (which SIM-KOI-002 covers).
Inspect JSON-RPC tools/call RESULT bodies on the wire for injection markers via NGFW content inspection.
Correlate the poisoned tool-result content hit with the agent's follow-on credential-file read from the same host into one incident (CR-KOI-0006).
